Appendix 60: Stability bounds, two-sided correction
and adverse tests
Contents of this appendix
1. What can be proved ............................................................................................................................................ 388
2. The anchor and its capacity ................................................................................................................................ 388
What arbitrage does and does not bound ........................................................................................................... 389
Finite resources disprove the unrestricted inference ........................................................................................... 389
3. Numerical assumptions and reproduction ........................................................................................................... 389

Stability bounds, two-sided correction and adverse tests
29 September 2026. Mathematical analysis and explicitly invented markets. No deployed pDAI
conversion facility, source-chain implementation or live execution is established by these experiments.
1. What can be proved
A path is a sequence of valid state transitions with exact asset identities, permissions, unit conversions
and funded outputs. If each transition accepts the preceding output, every obligation due is funded, and
the final state has the specified pDAI execution value, the composition reaches that value. This is a
conditional execution proposition. It does not prove the assumptions or make its initial funding free.
Source assets need only be accepted for a finite trade; their independent recoverability matters to losses
and repeatability.
The bridge models (Appendix 13) establish possible exclusive representations; the financing ledgers
(Appendix 42) show who pays for them; the route atlas (Appendix 51) identifies the separate transition
families. A route which returns the starting asset with a positive net surplus and settles its prescribed
obligations proves a profitable cycle for that participant. It does not prove a consolidated system profit if
another owned account bears the corresponding loss.
2. The anchor and its capacity
Let s > 0 be a fixed PLS reference in dollars over the execution interval. A proposed facility bids b = (1−δ)/
s PLS per pDAI and asks a = (1+δ)/s, where 0 ≤ δ < 1. It starts with spendable PLS R and deliverable pDAI H.
Its currently quoted capacities, before other obligations and costs, are
q_sell_to_facility ≤ R/b
q_buy_from_facility ≤ H.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 388

These are units of pDAI. If a user sells q directly at the bid, the facility's PLS falls by bq and pDAI rises by 
q; a purchase at the ask reverses these flows with aq. This explicitly supplies two-sided conversion while
the quoted inventories remain available. The capacity is shared by all users, not promised independently
to each simultaneous order.
With the PLS gas cost G, a direct sale nets reference value 1−δ−sG/q, and a direct purchase costs 1+δ+sG/q.
Thus a tolerance ε including gas requires δ+sG/q ≤ ε. Fixed gas makes arbitrarily small trades incompatible
with a tight all-in band unless someone funds that cost. A minimum size or fee subsidy is part of the
service definition.
This is a proposed funded conversion venue, not a pDAI token-contract redemption right found in the
audit. It is one explicit way to supply the missing closing trade. A different complete market route can
substitute if its executable quotes, timing and capacity provide the required terms.
What arbitrage does and does not bound
Let C_m(q) be PLS paid to buy q in a market and O_m(q) PLS received by selling q there, with market fees
and impact included. With feasible funding, facility capacity and total extra cost G, the two cycles are
profitable when
Buy market; sell facility:     bq − C_m(q) − G > 0.
Buy facility; sell market:     O_m(q) − aq − G > 0.
These are sufficient incentives at the stated size, not guarantees of inclusion or execution. Once no such
profitable cycle remains at a tested size, C_m(q) ≥ bq−G and O_m(q) ≤ aq+G. Notice what is not implied: these
cross-side bounds do not force every AMM sale quote above the facility bid, or every AMM purchase
quote below the ask. A market can have a wide spread with no profitable correction at that size. Users
need access to the facility or another best-execution route. A finite profitable correction also need not
eliminate all remaining opportunities at other sizes.
Finite resources disprove the unrestricted inference
With no intervening inflows or borrowing, a facility cannot pay more than R PLS, nor deliver more pDAI
than it holds. Multiple L2 token mints do not change that identity. Even an accepting constant-product
market with input reserve x and output reserve y pays only ya/(x+a) < y for finite input a in a fee-free
example; arbitrarily many input units do not create additional output inventory. Fees do not remove this
bound.
This is not a claim that an exact conversion rate is impossible under every specification. A fully funded
service can quote one price for a bounded supply and funded costs. It refutes the stronger inference that
controlled validators, nominal balances and arbitrage alone guarantee both directions for unrestricted
flow, time and adverse states. The claimed range must match actual resources.
3. Numerical assumptions and reproduction
The fresh manifest is Research/experiments/pulsechain_stability_review_20260929.json. The calculation uses 70-
digit Decimal arithmetic and checks token conservation with relative tolerance 10^-45. This is a
mathematical model, not integer EVM parity. Exact raw-token integer cycles remain in the separate pool-
cycle experiment (Appendix 47).
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 389

The initial AMM has 1,000,000 pDAI and 10,000,000,000 PLS, charges 0.3% on input, and starts at a
one-dollar reserve-ratio price using s = $0.0001. The treasury separately holds 300,000 pDAI and 
3,000,000,000 PLS. Its proposed bid is 9,900 PLS and ask 10,100 PLS per pDAI. The arbitrageur
owns sufficient working capital and pays 3,000 PLS gas per correction. There are no competing trades
during the correction.
An optional source funding witness stipulates that 1,000 exclusive source receipts are locked, 1,000
destination representations are issued and a buyer pays 3 billion already-owned PLS for them. That
finances the starting treasury cash without withdrawing the source investment. This is an accounting
witness, not a measured valuation, demonstrated buyer or new source-chain simulation. The 300,000
treasury pDAI is separately preowned.
Each market scenario starts from those balances, except the named unfunded controls. Repeated-
pressure scenarios apply eight successive equal shocks. Outside sellers are assumed to own the required
total pDAI at the beginning; buyers have the required PLS. No new pDAI is minted. The ledger includes
the pool, treasury, shock participant, arbitrageur and gas recipient.
The profit-maximizing single corrective trade can be solved analytically. Write current pool reserves as x
pDAI and y PLS and effective input fraction g = 0.997. After a sale shock, the arbitrageur spends
z_PLS = max(0, [sqrt(b*x*g*y) − y]/g)
buying pDAI to sell at the facility bid. Clip the output to R/b. After a buying shock, it buys pDAI at the
facility ask and sells it to the AMM:
z_pDAI = max(0, [sqrt(y*g*x/a) − x]/g), clipped to H.
The formulas differentiate gross cycle surplus; a fixed gas charge leaves the interior optimum unchanged
but can make execution unprofitable. No correction runs unless gross surplus exceeds gas. Debt-
financed capital would need its own cost and repayment account; none is assumed here.
Reproduce into a fresh file:
python3 Research/scripts/model_pulsechain_stability.py --manifest Research/experiments/
pulsechain_stability_review_20260929.json --output artifacts/pulsechain-stability-reproduction/results.json
The reference output is artifacts/pulsechain-stability-review-20260929/results.json. It records both input
hashes, complete balances, cycle profits, market probes, capacity controls, supply-depth examples, net-
income example, controller tests and all six simple cycle orientations in the specified four-asset graph.
4. Large selling: the complete account
A forced sale of 200,000 pDAI into the AMM pays 1,662,497,915.624479 PLS to its seller. The
reserve-ratio reference price falls from $1 to $0.694792. The arbitrageur then spends 
1,604,735,136.488911 PLS to acquire 193,199.495917 pDAI, sells that pDAI to the facility for 
1,912,675,009.573756 PLS, and keeps 307,936,873.084846 PLS after gas.
The treasury now holds 493,199.495917 pDAI and 1,087,324,990.426244 PLS. It has accumulated
pDAI and spent reserves. The arbitrageur's profit is not treasury income. The pool's resulting marginal
reference price is $0.987508. A 1,000-pDAI sale directly to the facility still pays $0.99 per pDAI before
gas, while that sale into the AMM averages $0.983572 before gas. The venues are not interchangeable
promises.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 390

The original seller received an average $0.831249 per pDAI before gas. Later correction does not repair
that earlier execution. This is a deliberately specified AMM shock, not a prediction that a best-execution
user would select it when a better funded direct bid is accessible. The distinction matters: post-trade
recovery and guaranteed in-band execution are different services.
A second equal AMM sale consumes the remaining facility PLS during partial correction, leaving a
marginal price of $0.832479. After that, further sales receive no facility-funded correction despite the
treasury owning more pDAI. The eight-shock stress finishes near $0.190264 in this model. These are
finite initial inventories with no income or new funding, not a forecast. The unfunded-bid control
performs no correction after the first shock.
The optimum was checked independently against neighboring trade sizes and its closed surplus. Every
step reconciles pool, treasury, outside seller, arbitrageur and gas-recipient token movements. Extra
source balances alone change none of these cash flows; a separately funded sale or financing would
have to replenish PLS before another bid can pay.
5. Large buying: the opposite inventory obligation
Reset the initial state. A buyer spends 2,000,000,000 PLS into the AMM, receiving 166,249.791562
pDAI and moving its marginal price to $1.43928. The arbitrageur buys 160,523.354012 pDAI from
the facility for 1,621,285,875.520206 PLS, then sells it into the premium AMM for 
1,932,498,372.003088 PLS. After gas it earns 311,209,496.482882 PLS.
The treasury now has 139,476.645988 pDAI and 4,621,285,875.520206 PLS. The marginal AMM
price is $1.012548. Its 1,000-pDAI purchase quote is $1.016618 per pDAI before gas, while the facility
still asks $1.01. Again, access to the better route matters. The initial AMM buyer paid about $1.203009
per pDAI before gas; later correction does not refund that price impact.
A second equal buying shock exhausts the facility's remaining pDAI during partial correction, despite its
growing PLS reserve. Its marginal price remains $1.066216; after eight shocks without replenishment it
reaches about $4.968517. The unfunded-ask control cannot correct the first shock. The analytical buy
optimum and token conservation were checked as for selling.
Buying pressure can therefore fund later bids, while selling pressure can replenish inventory for later
asks. This is a useful two-sided interaction, not proof that flows arrive in the required order or that all
acquired inventory will be resold at a gain. Additional pDAI delivery requires exact-token stock, a valid
withdrawal or issuance route, or borrowing with a return obligation. New FRAX issuance cannot be
silently substituted for it.
6. Favorable recovery, income and supply concentration
A separate explicit batch, Research/experiments/pulsechain_stability_recovery_20260929.json, starts with the
actual modeled pool and treasury left by the large-sale case. Its funding witness records the preceding
output hash. A subsequent outside purchase of 2 billion PLS creates another profitable correction: the
treasury sells 156,140.782347 pDAI, receives 1,577,021,901.705877 PLS, and ends with 
337,058.713569 pDAI and 2,664,346,892.132120 PLS. The arbitrageur earns 
292,741,760.017276 PLS after gas. The cash reserve has substantially recovered, while it remains
below its original 3-billion-PLS level and inventory remains above its original 300,000 pDAI. Their
combined value requires a stated valuation; the cash change alone is not total profit.
This shows the useful alternation rather than assuming it. Outside funded buying provides the cash; the
timing and occurrence of that buying are premises. Reproduce with the same script, the recovery
manifest and a fresh output file. The reference result is artifacts/pulsechain-stability-review-20260929/
recovery-results.json.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 391

The original batch also reproduces the accumulation appendix's three exact price-impact cases: halved
selling at retained depth improves execution; halved selling with 90% less depth worsens it. A separate
income calculation produces $240,000 gross attributable external LP fees, $40,000 collected interest
and $80,000 funding/operating costs. Net income is $200,000 without losses, but −$50,000 with 
$250,000 realized losses. The favorable case is in the recovery batch; neither injects this income into
the market simulation. Generation, collection and the time available for reinvestment must be
separately specified before claiming further support capacity.
The accumulation study (Appendix 65) distinguishes physical token balances, beneficial claims, debt,
external wallet float and potential selling through borrowing or withdrawal. Concentration can reduce
one seller cohort's inventory without permanently removing assets from trading.
7. Corrective feedback needs a timing rule
The favorable economic feedback is not itself a control law. T o expose the role of response strength and
delay, consider a deliberately simplified local model. Let e_t be deviation from the target and k the
proportional response, with unit-normalized price impact and no new shock or capacity saturation:
Immediate correction: e_(t+1) = (1−k)e_t.
One-step delay:        e_(t+1) = e_t − k e_(t−1).
Immediate correction contracts when 0 < k < 2. With one-step delay the characteristic equation is 
λ²−λ+k=0; both roots lie inside the unit circle exactly when 0 < k < 1. For k > 1/4, their magnitude is sqrt(k).
Thus k=1.2 is stable without delay but unstable with this delay. T wo independently chosen delayed
controllers of gain 0.6, acting on the same error, have combined gain 1.2; individually stable policies
need not be stable together.
The batch checks these roots and 40-step numerical sequences. Divergent values outside the initial
neighborhood are mathematical diagnostics, not forecast pDAI prices. This linear toy omits AMM
curvature, saturation, noise, arbitrage competition and state-dependent liquidity. It refutes the assertion
that stronger or more coordinated responses must always improve stability; it does not calibrate an
actual controller.
A production proposal would need explicit quote updates, inventory budgets, response limits, shared
commitments, oracle validity and finality assumptions. Remote funds cannot serve an immediate quote
until delivered or credibly advanced. Under an outage or exhausted capacity the service must stop
promising unavailable execution; that is a failure of an unconditional peg claim, even if the bounded
service behaves as specified. No controller implementation is claimed in this paper.
8. Reference, collateral and liabilities
The original 3-billion-PLS reserve supports at most 303,030.303030 pDAI at the $0.99 reference bid
and s=$0.0001, before costs and other commitments. If PLS halves in reference value, the same reserve's
capacity halves to 151,515.151515 pDAI. At s=$0.00001, capacity is 30,303.030303 pDAI. These are
stressed quote budgets, not simultaneous commitments to be added.
If a controller quotes using s_hat while the relevant true reference is s, its nominal $0.99 payout has true
reference value 0.99*s/s_hat before costs. An erroneous twofold overstatement of PLS value therefore
pays only $0.495 of that reference per pDAI. The reference cannot be validated merely by a market
whose target price it is supposed to support.
Collateral haircut, borrowing limits and maturity matter as much as its marked balance. Realizable claim
proceeds L, support outflows W, costs C and debt payments due D_due must satisfy R + L ≥ W + C + D_due
before the relevant payments. A later expected return does not repair an earlier shortfall. Future
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 392

principal does not all have to be repaid immediately; it remains a later obligation with its own liquidity
test. Internal claims cancel on consolidation. Minting claims on self-issued balances can produce
accepted trades, but marking those claims at the target cannot prove the resources required to defend
it.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 393

Immediate correction contracts when 0 < k < 2. With one-step delay the characteristic equation is 
λ²−λ+k=0; both roots lie inside the unit circle exactly when 0 < k < 1. For k > 1/4, their magnitude is sqrt(k).
Thus k=1.2 is stable without delay but unstable with this delay. T wo independently chosen delayed
controllers of gain 0.6, acting on the same error, have combined gain 1.2; individually stable policies
need not be stable together.
The batch checks these roots and 40-step numerical sequences. Divergent values outside the initial
neighborhood are mathematical diagnostics, not forecast pDAI prices. This linear toy omits AMM
curvature, saturation, noise, arbitrage competition and state-dependent liquidity. It refutes the assertion
that stronger or more coordinated responses must always improve stability; it does not calibrate an
actual controller.
A production proposal would need explicit quote updates, inventory budgets, response limits, shared
commitments, oracle validity and finality assumptions. Remote funds cannot serve an immediate quote
until delivered or credibly advanced. Under an outage or exhausted capacity the service must stop
promising unavailable execution; that is a failure of an unconditional peg claim, even if the bounded
service behaves as specified. No controller implementation is claimed in this paper.
8. Reference, collateral and liabilities
The original 3-billion-PLS reserve supports at most 303,030.303030 pDAI at the $0.99 reference bid
and s=$0.0001, before costs and other commitments. If PLS halves in reference value, the same reserve's
capacity halves to 151,515.151515 pDAI. At s=$0.00001, capacity is 30,303.030303 pDAI. These are
stressed quote budgets, not simultaneous commitments to be added.
If a controller quotes using s_hat while the relevant true reference is s, its nominal $0.99 payout has true
reference value 0.99*s/s_hat before costs. An erroneous twofold overstatement of PLS value therefore
pays only $0.495 of that reference per pDAI. The reference cannot be validated merely by a market
whose target price it is supposed to support.
Collateral haircut, borrowing limits and maturity matter as much as its marked balance. Realizable claim
proceeds L, support outflows W, costs C and debt payments due D_due must satisfy R + L ≥ W + C + D_due
before the relevant payments. A later expected return does not repair an earlier shortfall. Future
